Question: Jo and Blair take turns counting from \(1\) to one more than the last number said by the other person. Jo starts by saying “\(1\)”, so Blair follows by saying “\(1,\) \(2\)”. Jo then says “\(1,\) \(2,\) \(3\)”, and so on. What number is spoken in position \(53\)?
Solution:
Each turn ends one number later than the preceding turn, so turn \(n\) consists of \(1,2,\ldots,n\) and contains \(n\) spoken numbers. We need to count all entries in earlier turns before locating position \(53\).

The first nine turns contain
\[
1+2+\cdots+9=\frac{9(1+9)}2=45
\]
spoken numbers. The tenth turn adds ten more, bringing the total to \(55\). Since \(45<53\le55\), position \(53\) lies in the tenth turn. It is entry \(53-45=8\) of that turn, whose entries start at \(1\). Therefore the number spoken is \(\boxed{8}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
